blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Wearable fall detection is hampered by rare fall events, scarce labeled IMU data, and the cost of training deep models on large, imbalanced corpora. Existing methods either rely on hand-crafted features with shallow classifiers, which limits learning from raw signals, or train deep networks on full datasets that require re-sampling to counter class skew and demand substantial data and compute. To address this, we propose a novel Fall detection framework via Normalized-gradient and Embedding matched Synthetic Time-frequency condensation, dubbed FALLNEST, a data-centric approach that distills large, imbalanced IMU datasets into tiny, class-balanced synthetic training sets. Building on dual-domain time-series condensation (CondTSC), FALLNEST introduces a fall-specific 7-channel input with accelerometer vector magnitude, class-balanced K-Means initialization, and normalized gradient matching with gradient clipping, combined with MMD-based embedding alignment and multi-view Fourier-domain augmentation, so that class balance arises from the condensed set itself rather than from re-sampling. We evaluate on SisFall, KFall, and MobiFall using strict subject-wise splits and naturally imbalanced test sets, reporting accuracy, Macro-F1, and PR-AUC over five seeds. A 102K-parameter TinyCNN trained on only 32 to 146 synthetic windows (about only 1% of the training windows) reaches 93.5-95.8% mean accuracy and 0.89-0.98 PR-AUC, with standard deviations of 1.0-1.7% in accuracy, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach.
blocks.zh: 可穿戴的倒地探测因罕见的倒地事件而受阻,被贴上IMU标签的数据稀少,在大型不平衡的蝎子上训练深层模型的成本也很高. 现有方法要么依靠手制特征和浅分仪,这些特征限制了从原始信号中学习,要么在需要再作取样的完整数据集上训练深分网络,以对抗类分仪并需要大量数据和计算. 为了解决这个问题,我们提出一个新的Fall检测框架,通过正常升级和嵌入匹配的Synthetic Time-频率收缩,被誉为FALLNEST,一种以数据为中心的方法,将庞大的,不平衡的IMU数据集分解成细小的,阶级平衡的合成培训集. 在双域时间序列收缩(CondTSC)的基础上,FALLNEST引入了带有加速计矢量级的秋季特异性7道输入,类平衡K-Means初始化,并实现梯度相匹配与梯度剪接的常态相匹配,并结合了基于MMD的嵌入对接和多视图Fourier-domain增生,因此类平衡来自于收缩的设定本身,而不是从再采样. 我们用严格的主题划分和自然不平衡的测试集、报告准确性、Macro-F1和PR-AUC来评价SisFall、KFall和MobiFall。 102K-参数的TinyCNN只培训了32至146个合成窗口(约占培训窗口的1%),达到93.5-95.8%的中精度和0.89-0.98 PR-AUC,标准偏差为1.0-1.7%的精度,证明了我们的方法的有效性.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults and a recurring hazard in workplaces [ 5 ] , and wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) enable continuous, unobtrusive monitoring [ 8 ] . Learning a reliable fall detector from IMU data is hard for two reasons. Falls are rare compared with activities of daily living (ADLs), so labeled data are scarce and skewed [ 7 ] , and wearables operate under tight power, memory, and processing budgets [ 2 ] . The usual remedies for skew, oversampling and augmentation, enlarge the training set and its compute cost. Lightweight pipelines instead rely on hand-crafted features, for example spectral features from 25 Hz IMU data fed to a feed-forward network [ 3 ] , which limits learning from raw signals. Deep networks learn features automatically and reach near-perfect accuracy on standard benchmarks [ 14 , 1 , 6 ] , but need large imbalanced training sets, substantial compute, and often re-sampling. Dataset condensation distills a large dataset into a small synthetic set that retains its training value [ 11 ] . It has mainly been studied on images, and its time-series extension [ 4 ] was not evaluated on wearable fall detection under subject-wise splits with naturally imbalanced test sets. We propose Fall detection framework via N ormalized-gradient and E mbedding-matched S ynthetic T ime–frequency condensation ( FallNest ), which shrinks the training data rather than the model. It distills a large, imbalanced IMU dataset into a tiny, class-balanced synthetic set on which a lightweight CNN learns discriminative fall patterns. FallNest builds on CondTSC [ 4 ] and differs in four ways: (i) a fall-specific 7-channel input (tri-axial accelerometer, tri-axial gyroscope, accelerometer vector magnitude); (ii) class-balanced K-Means initialization, which balances the set by construction; (iii) normalized gradient matching with gradient clipping, which stabilizes optimization across datasets of very different sizes; and (iv) strict subject-wise splits with naturally imbalanced test sets. Raw signals are left unfiltered so that sharp impact peaks are preserved. On SisFall [ 9 ] , KFall [ 12 ] , and MobiFall [ 10 ] , a 102 K-parameter TinyCNN trained on 32 to 146 synthetic windows (about 1% of the training windows) reaches 93.5 to 95.8% mean accuracy and 0.89 to 0.98 PR-AUC over five seeds. The roughly 100-fold reduction applies to the downstream training set, not to the data accessed during condensation, which uses all of 𝒯 \mathcal{T} ; a real validation set only selects the checkpoint. Our contributions are: a dual-domain condensation framework that turns imbalanced IMU recordings into compact, class-balanced training sets without re-sampling; a dual-objective scheme pairing normalized, clipped gradient matching with MMD alignment in both domains, plus multi-view Fourier augmentation; and a rigorous evaluation protocol (subject-wise splits, natural test priors, accuracy, Macro-F1, PR-AUC over five seeds) with ablations and a PCA analysis of real versus synthetic embeddings. All datasets are public, and code will be released upon acceptance.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: FallNest condenses a large, imbalanced IMU training set into a tiny, class-balanced synthetic set, and a lightweight classifier is trained on that set alone (Fig. 1 ). Recordings become subject-disjoint windows; a balanced synthetic set is initialized with class-wise K-Means and refined in time and frequency domains through four augmented views by a joint normalized gradient-matching and MMD objective (Alg. 1 ). A TinyCNN is then trained on the condensed set ( 𝒮 \mathcal{S} ), selected on a real validation set ( 𝒱 \mathcal{V} ), and evaluated on a subject-independent, naturally imbalanced test set ( 𝒯 test \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{test}} ).

\SubSection Downstream Training, Backbone, and Evaluation



A fresh TinyCNN is trained on 𝒮 \mathcal{S} only (cross-entropy, 100 epochs, Adam lr 0.001 0.001 , batch size 16). Each backbone has three Conv1D–BatchNorm–ReLU blocks, adaptive average pooling, and a fully connected layer; the deployed classifier is the time-domain TinyCNN alone, and the frequency branch is used only during condensation. The model has 102 K parameters ( ≈ \approx 400 KB in float32) and needs about 103 M MACs ( L = 1000 L{=}1000 ) to 206 M MACs ( L = 2000 L{=}2000 ) per inference, with 2.15 ms median CPU latency (Kaggle CPU, single-threaded PyTorch, batch size 1). Table 2 reports test Accuracy, Macro-F1, and PR-AUC. Using only 1% of training windows, FallNest achieves 93.5–95.8% accuracy and 0.891–0.975 PR-AUC, exceeding the always-ADL accuracy baselines by 9.7, 20.7, and 30.3 percentage points on SisFall, MobiFall, and KFall, respectively. Compared with full-data training, accuracy drops by 6.4, 4.5, and 3.6 points, respectively; SisFall also shows the largest PR-AUC reduction (0.999 to 0.891).

blocks.en:
\SubSection Comparison with Full-Data Methods

Table 2 lists recent full-data methods, which report 98–99.8% accuracy on these datasets, with the FallNest rows for the same datasets below. Each published row gives one metric only, accuracy for most methods and PR-AUC for the BiLSTM–BiGRU model, so a full comparison on both metrics is not possible. Against these methods, FallNest gives up about 3–6 points of accuracy (for example 99.3% versus 93.5% on SisFall) while using about two orders of magnitude fewer training windows. The comparison is not like for like, because published protocols differ in splitting, class balance, and metrics. LiteFallNet [ 6 ] and BiLSTM–BiGRU [ 1 ] use random window-level splits, which can inflate results through temporal leakage, whereas [ 14 ] and [ 13 ] use variants of subject-wise cross-validation. One could suspect that published numbers are inflated by window-level splits, but our own full-data TinyCNN under strict subject-wise splitting reaches 99.85%, 100.00%, and 99.39%, at the level of the published methods, so leakage is not the main explanation. These benchmarks appear saturated under either protocol, and the 3–6 point gap is mostly the price of the 100-fold data reduction. We do not claim parity with full-data training. The case for condensation is use cases in which storing or processing the full corpus is impractical, such as rapid prototyping or on-device personalization.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We proposed Fall detection framework via N ormalized-gradient and E mbedding-matched S ynthetic T ime–frequency condensation ( FallNest ), a dual-domain dataset condensation framework for wearable fall detection that distills a large, imbalanced IMU training set into a tiny, class-balanced synthetic set using class-balanced K-Means initialization, a 7-channel input with AVM, normalized and clipped gradient matching with MMD alignment, and multi-view Fourier augmentation. Under strict subject-wise splits and naturally imbalanced test sets, a 102 K-parameter TinyCNN trained on 32 to 146 synthetic windows (about 1% of the training windows) reaches 93.5–95.8% mean accuracy and 0.89–0.98 PR-AUC over five seeds, 3.6 to 6.4 points below full-data training. The ablations indicate that K-Means initialization, multi-view augmentation, and the combined loss each matter, most clearly where the synthetic set is smallest. Inference cost was measured on a CPU only; future work includes false-alarm analysis on free-living data and microcontroller deployment.
blocks.zh: 我们提出通过 N ormalized-gradition 和 E mbedding- matched S ynthetic T ime – 频率收缩(FallNest)的Fall检测框架,一个可穿戴秋季检测的双域数据集收缩框架,利用班级平衡的 K- Means 初始化,将一个大型不平衡的IMU 培训集分解成一个小而班级平衡的合成集,一个7个频道输入AVM,与 MMD 相匹配的规范化和剪接梯度匹配,以及多视图的 Fourier 增强. 在严格按主题划分和自然不平衡的测试组下,在32至146个合成窗口(约占培训窗口的1%)上培训的102个K-参数TinyCNN达到93.5-95.8%的精度,在5个种子中达到0.89-0.98的PR-AUC,低于完整数据培训的3.6至6.4分。 活化表明K-Means初始化,多视增强,以及每个物质的综合损失,最明显的是合成集最小的地方. 推论成本只用CPU计量;今后的工作包括对自由活数据的错误警报分析和微控制器部署.
